## Oneway OS: Business Management Platform

Source: https://onewayos.com/

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

OS

Oneway OS.

Run a business, a community or a place from one operating system: its Systems, its Brain and its website.

Business OS is available by contact in the Closed Selective Server Beta, starting in New York City.

Talk to us

Systems

One System for each part of the work.

Core Systems every business uses, and industry Systems that bring them along.

Core Systems
Customers, stock, assets and upkeep, bookings, staff schedules and messages.

Industry Systems
Hotels, restaurants, casinos, property, HVAC and more, each installing the core Systems it needs.

One record each
A customer, a room or a part is one record every System reads.

Oneway CRM
Oneway Inventory Management
Oneway Asset Management
Oneway Hotel Operations
Oneway HVAC Service Operations

The Brain

It reads the whole business, and asks before it acts.

Recommends
What needs a person now, from every System's records.

A person decides
Nothing it proposes happens until someone with the role says yes.

Websites

Your site, designed from boxes at the side.

Fifteen layouts
Tried live at a PC's width and a phone's before anything changes.

Width, spacing, type and corners
Each one press; kept only when you keep it.

The same Center in the App
The people who follow you see the same place.

Run it from one place.
Talk to us The Oneway App

## Oneway Asset Management and Maintenance

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/asset-management

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Asset Management
Core System

Asset Management.

Every thing your business owns, who has it, what it costs, and the work that keeps it running.

The base every physical System runs on: Hotel Operations, Restaurant Operations, Property Management, HVAC and more.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta.

Talk to us

Asset Management in Oneway OS, with sample records.

The register

Anything, in your own words.

Every thing, one register
Found by words, tag, code, kind, place or state; changed many at a time.

Where it stands
Places inside places, and things inside things; moving one moves what it holds.

A QR code for each
Printed in house; scanning it opens the thing in the OS.

Lent and returned
Checked out to a person until a day, never twice; back with its condition.

Bought and warranted
Price, supplier, warranty and useful life; warranties ending in 90 days listed.

A guided audit
Walked place by place, with what was not found.

The register's report, the map of every thing by place, and the work each department does.

Maintenance

Kept working, and the cost known.

Work orders
Handed to whoever is on the clock with the fewest open, who is told on their phone.

Closed with the proof
Parts, cost, hours and pictures of the fix, on the thing's own record.

Last time this happened
The next person sees what fixed it before, picture and all.

Preventive work that opens itself
Every so many days, or by a meter's reading; on time, late and overdue said.

Reported once
Guests, members and staff report from the App and are told when it is fixed.

Sensors feeding meters
A meter read from the equipment itself, through its sensors feed.

Cost and condition

Repair it or replace it.

Condition and state, apart
Working, degraded or failed, and in or out of service; out of order leaves what can be sold.

Downtime, every span
Hours down in the last 90 days and in all, from the thing's own history.

Reliability
Mean time between failures and to repair, and the least reliable things.

Cost of ownership
Price plus every repair, book value, and when replacing is worth weighing.

A history nobody rewrites
Every change, who, when and why.

Scheduled reports
The report sent to the owners in Oneway on its day, and the register as a sheet.

The base

One physical world under every System.

A hotel's rooms, a casino's machines and a customer's furnace are all assets. Each industry System adds its own kinds of things and its own work; the condition, history and upkeep are the same everywhere.

Each industry has its own System
Its own install, screens and acts, on these assets.

Installed together
Installing Hotel Operations installs Asset Management, Reservations and Maintenance with it.

How it works

A thing, and everything that happens to it.

Add it
By hand, from a spreadsheet or a QR label.

Use it
Booked, lent, sold or worked on.

Keep it working
Work orders and preventive upkeep on the thing.

Know its cost
Downtime, repairs and the case to replace it.

Who it is for

Every place that owns things.

Hotels and resorts
Rooms, elevators, kitchens and plant.

Venues and casinos
Machines, tables and the floor.

Property managers
Units and what is inside them.

Gyms, schools and offices
Equipment, rooms and vehicles.

Comes with these Systems

Casino Operations System
Events
Oneway Hotel Operations
Oneway Inventory Management
Maintenance
Property Management System
Restaurant Operations System

Know every thing you own.
Talk to us Business OS

## Oneway CRM | Customer Relationship Management

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/crm

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Oneway CRM
Core System

Oneway CRM.

Every customer's whole story, built from what they actually do with your business.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Oneway CRM in Oneway OS, with sample records.

The record

One customer, one story.

Bookings, stays, orders, posts and messages land on the same record, so nobody types a history in.

A timeline per customer
Notes, deals and their moves, stays, orders paid, rewards and messages, newest first.

Tags, an owner and your own fields
Words, numbers, dates and lists of your own, filtered and exported.

Consent, said once
Email, texts and calls each agreed or refused. Do-not-contact stops every campaign and audience.

Joined on evidence
Two records become one only on a confirmed address or id, never on a name.

Duplicates merged
Found by email, phone or name and merged by an owner, with every deal carried over.

Auto-tags by rule
Regulars and big spenders tagged from what they did.
Planned

Each customer's record: the timeline, the deals, the follow-ups and their consent.

Pipeline

From the first message to the signed deal.

Deals at six stages, each with its chance to close and what it is worth.

Deals and stages
Lead, qualified, proposal, negotiation, won and lost, with value and weighted value.

Won and lost, with why
The last 90 days' win rate, the reasons deals were lost, each owner's share.

Follow-ups that land
A due day and hour, handed to a person who is told, on their own Workspace.

Leads from your own book
People who booked with their account and are not on your list, made customers in one press.

Your own stages and several pipelines
Stages named your way, a pipeline per kind of sale.
Planned

A reminder at the hour
A follow-up that rings when it is due.
Planned

Lists and data

Your customers, yours to move.

Saved lists that keep up
By tag, owner, company, stage, consent or words, counted again every time.

Search everything
Names, addresses, phones, companies, tags and notes.

Import and export
A CSV in, each refused row named; every column out, a list or a filter at a time.

The report
Pipeline by stage, won and lost, follow-ups open, overdue and done.

Email from the CRM
Sequences, templates and tracking.
Planned

Web forms
Your site's forms making contacts.
Planned

The difference

A CRM that does not need feeding.

Most CRMs are only as good as what someone types in. Oneway CRM is fed by the business itself.

Part of the business
Reservations, rewards, orders and messages write to the same customer. Nothing to sync.

Their own profile, live
A customer on Oneway keeps their name and face current themselves.

Private by default
Staff see customers only when their role works with them. Strangers see nothing.

How it works

From what happened to who to call.

Something happens
A booking, a visit, an order or a message.

It finds its customer
On evidence: the same address or id.

The record moves
Its story, its deals and its tags.

The team acts
Follow-ups due land on the right person.

Who it is for

Any business people come back to.

Hotels and resorts
Repeat guests known before they arrive.

Restaurants
Regulars, their table and their preferences.

Services and practices
Clients and the next appointment owed.

Venues and clubs
Members, groups and their bookings.

Comes with these Systems

Casino Operations System
Oneway Hotel Operations
Restaurant Operations System

Know your customers by what they do.
Talk to us Business OS

## Oneway Hotel Operations | Hotel Management System

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/hotel-operations

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Hotel Operations
Industry System

Hotel Operations.

The book, the desk, the night audit, the accounts and housekeeping, for a hotel run from one place.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Hotel Operations in Oneway OS, with sample records.

The book

From the rate to the room.

Stays
Booked by room and dates; what is left to sell, by type and night.

Rates
A rate ladder per room type; a type closed to sale on chosen dates.

Group blocks
Rooms held to a cut-off, released after, tied to the group's event.

Taxes and terms
The room taxes a stay is charged, and the registration card's words.

The book you have today
An export from your current system, brought in as stays.

Online travel agencies
Rooms and rates sent to booking sites, bookings back.
Planned

The nights ahead on the books, and what each department does next.

Front desk

The desk's whole day.

Arrivals, in house, due out
Every room's state beside the guests.

Check in, check out, move
Deposits recorded, rooms moved before or during the stay.

Charges
Posted by the desk, or waiting from the point of sale for one press.

The night audit
Each night's room charges and taxes, posted by your rules.

The numbers
Occupancy, ADR and RevPAR beside the same night last year.

Folios and accounts

Every charge, and who pays it.

Oneway records money and never moves it.

Routing
A stay's charges sent to a house account or another folio.

House accounts
Billed as numbered invoices, paid oldest first, closed.

Disputes and write-offs
Each with who and why.

Split a bill by payer
Separate windows on one folio.
Planned

Recurring and batch charges
A charge that repeats, or one charge to many accounts.
Planned

Housekeeping

Clean, inspected, and known.

Room status from a phone
Dirty, cleaned, inspected, ready; a room sells only once inspected.

Rooms to clean
Each assigned to a person, on their phone.

Out of order
Taken out of sale with its reason, and returned to service.

Traces
A note about a stay for a department on a day, marked done.

Runs on Asset Management

Every room is an asset.

Hotel Operations is its own System, with its own install, screens and acts. Its rooms are assets, so condition, history and upkeep are the same records engineering works on.

Out of order is not out of service
Out of order leaves what can be sold; out of service stays in the count.

Brings what a hotel needs
Reservations, Maintenance and Oneway CRM come with it.

How it works

A stay, from booking to the audit.

Booked
A room, dates and a rate.

Checked in
The deposit on the folio.

In the house
Charges posted, traces worked.

Audited
The night posted, the numbers read.

Who it is for

Hotels run from one place.

Independent hotels
The book, the desk and the accounts in one System.

Resorts
Hotel, restaurants and casino on one Center.

Groups of hotels
Each property its own Center, run the same way.

Inns and boutique hotels
Fewer rooms, the same discipline.

Runs on

Oneway Asset Management

Brings with it

Reservations System
Maintenance
Oneway CRM

Run your hotel from one place.
Talk to us Business OS

## Oneway HVAC | Field Service Software for HVAC

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/hvac

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › HVAC Service Operations
Industry System

HVAC Service Operations.

From the first call to the finished job, every unit's history, and the agreements that keep customers coming back.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

HVAC Service Operations in Oneway OS, with sample records.

Calls and dispatch

Every call is a job from the first minute.

Take a call
A returning customer or a new one, the service address kept with them.

Four kinds of job
Service call, maintenance visit, install or estimate, in the caller's words.

Arrival windows
One to four hours on your own clock; moved, and the tech moves with it.

Send a tech
Told on their phone at once; their shift and other jobs checked first.

The dispatch board
Each tech's shift and jobs in order, and the jobs still waiting.

Dispatch on a map
Drag a job onto a tech, in route order.
Planned

The board: jobs today, waiting for a tech, visits due and agreements ending.

In the field

The tech's day, on their phone.

My day
The shift, and each job with its address and window.

Start and finish from the phone
What was done, the parts used and pictures; the office sees it at once.

The customer's sign-off
Their acknowledgment, typed and timed.

Estimates and invoice amounts
Recorded on the job; Oneway never charges a card.

On my way
The customer told the tech is coming.
Planned

A price book
Line items, and good-better-best options.
Planned

Equipment and agreements

Every unit's history, every renewal on time.

Units on record
Make, model, serial, install year, refrigerant, tonnage and warranty.

Last time this happened
A job on a unit arrives knowing everything it has been through.

Service agreements
A plan, its yearly value, its term and visits, and the units it covers.

Visits that book themselves
Due visits on the board, booked as maintenance jobs on the unit.

Renewals
Agreements ending in 60 days listed, renewed from the day the old one ends.

Recurring billing
Agreements billed on their own.
Planned

Runs on Asset Management

Every furnace is an asset.

HVAC Service Operations is its own System with its own install and screens. Each customer's unit is an asset, so its history, condition and upkeep are kept the way every physical thing on Oneway is.

The shop's own things too
Trucks, tools and parts in the same register.

Brings what a service company needs
Service Management, Maintenance and Asset Management come with it.

How it works

From the call to the next visit.

A call comes in
The customer, the address, the problem.

A tech is sent
In a window that fits their shift.

The job is done
What fixed it, on the unit's record.

The next visit
Booked from the agreement, renewed on time.

Who it is for

Shops that keep homes and buildings comfortable.

Residential HVAC
Furnaces, air conditioners and heat pumps.

Commercial service
Rooftop units and walk-in coolers.

Plumbing and electrical
The same calls, jobs and agreements.

Owner-operators
One truck today, a fleet later.

Runs on

Oneway Asset Management

Brings with it

Maintenance

Run your service company from one place.
Talk to us Business OS

## Oneway Inventory Management

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/inventory

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Inventory Management
Core System

Inventory Management.

What you hold, where it is, what it cost and what is running out, in one history every department writes to.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Inventory Management in Oneway OS, with sample records.

Stock

Every item, counted the same way.

Items, packs and variants
A unit, pack sizes, a SKU and a barcode; sizes and colours each counted on their own.

By place and by shelf
Stock where it actually sits, moved between places in one step.

Counts
A whole place or item by item; the difference shown at once, booked by an owner.

Waste with a reason
Spoiled, damaged, expired, lost or used in house, each in dollars.

One history
Every change kept for good; on hand is never typed over.

Lots and expiry
Each delivery's lot and the day it expires.
Planned

Every item is one of the business's things: on the map by place, with its own history.

Ordering

Running low, before it runs out.

Par and reorder points
Per place or for the whole business; owners told once when it runs low.

Orders drafted for you
What is low, onto its supplier's order, filled to par and rounded to the pack.

Approved, received, closed
An owner approves; it arrives in part or in full; what never came is said.

Suppliers measured
Their stated lead time beside the real one, fill rate and on-time count.

Sending orders to suppliers
A purchase order by email or PDF.
Planned

A demand forecast
When each item will run out at today's pace, and when to order.

Where it goes

Used by the work that used it.

Parts on a work order
Their cost lands on the repair, and on the thing it fixed.

Parts installed in things
A part's one life: in stock, installed, removed, repaired or disposed of.

Sold out, everywhere
A product at zero shows Sold out in the Shop and the App, and returns with new stock.

Sales from your point of sale
Square, Shopify, Clover, Toast and Lightspeed sales take stock by SKU.
Planned

Every property at once
On hand, low items and orders across properties, and stock sent between them.

Recipes and plate cost
What a dish uses, and what it costs to make.
Planned

The difference

One stock for the whole business.

Kitchen tools count the kitchen; maintenance tools count parts. Here every department writes to one history.

Tied to the work
A part used on a repair is on that repair, and on the thing it fixed.

Tied to the customer
What is out reaches the Shop and the App, not only the storeroom.

Every item is a thing you own
Stock lives in Asset Management's register, on the same map.

How it works

A movement, every time.

It arrives
Received against its order, at the invoice's cost.

It is kept
On a shelf in a place, counted when you count.

It is used
By a sale, a department or a repair.

It is replaced
Below par, an order is drafted for you to approve.

Who it is for

Anyone who keeps things on a shelf.

Hotels
Linen, amenities and engineering's parts.

Restaurants and bars
Food and drink, counted and costed.

Shops
What is for sale, and what is left.

Service companies
The parts every truck carries.

Know what you have before you run out.
